name: PW Digital Gateway
note: Approved in 2023 (4-3-1) but the rezoning was judicially voided over defective hearing notice; county and developer dropped their appeals in 2026, ending the project as approved.

name: Plaza 500 (Lincolnia)
note: By-right data center on the 34-acre 6299 Edsall Road site; the required substation faces a Fairfax County Planning Commission Public Facilities (2232) review on Sept 24, 2026 amid organized opposition.

name: Project Iron Spur
note: ~129-acre hyperscale campus proposed across from Rural Hall town hall; Forsyth County Planning Board recommended denial. Commissioners held the public hearing July 30, 2026 - decision pending.

name: Meta Hyperion
note: Approved and under construction - a ~5 GW, ~$27B campus. Louisiana approved new Entergy natural-gas generation to serve it; ratepayer cost allocation is the live fight, not the siting.

name: Burkhalter Road data center (4AM Development)
note: Two-story 230,000 sq ft data center plus a 32,000 sq ft substation on ~26.5 acres at 6539 Burkhalter Road (R-4 residential to Office & Business rezoning). Planning Commission recommended approval 5-1; City Council decides Aug 18, 2026. Bulloch County, separately, has been extending data-center moratoriums.

name: West Erwin Street data center (Barrio Resources)
note: Special use permit for a bitcoin-mining data center on ~1.92 acres near downtown (W. Erwin St & N. Ross Ave) denied 5-2 by the Planning & Zoning Commission - staff found it inconsistent with the Future Land Use Map and comprehensive plan, after resident opposition over water, noise, and proximity to homes. Applicant may appeal.

name: Aligned Data Centers - Pataskala industrial park
note: 200 MW campus in three buildings on ~89 acres at Broad St SW & Mink St SW. Planning & Zoning recommended rejection 5-2 after protests filled City Hall; City Council decides Aug 25, 2026 (5:30 p.m.). Council has separately advanced a ballot measure that could ban large data centers.

name: King of Prussia campus (MLP Ventures)
note: Five-site, 4.6M sq ft campus; Board of Supervisors denied extension requests and preliminary land development proposals Aug 14, 2026. Developer filed lawsuit; judge vacated injunction, finding township review fair. 20,000-signature petition against. Developer plans to appeal.

name: AWS Calvert Technology Center
note: Eight data center buildings (266,000-332,000 sq ft each) proposed at 1650 Calvert Cliffs Parkway on Constellation-owned parcels near the Calvert Cliffs nuclear plant. AWS formally withdrew the concept site plan on Aug 4, 2026 - after first-round county review comments and before any resubmission. Timeline documented on the county's own project page.

name: xAI Colossus
note: Operating and expanding (~$20B, ~2 GW ambition). The live fight is air quality: on-site gas turbines in southwest Memphis - an area already failing federal ozone standards - drew a Clean Air Act suit. Environmental groups' tracking put unpermitted turbines at 27 in Feb 2026, growing to 59 by mid-2026 across the Colossus complex (incl. Colossus 2 in Southaven, MS).

name: Nordson campus data center (Cervenka)
note: Use variance to convert three newer buildings on the longtime Nordson Corporation campus into a data center complex - denied by the Board of Zoning Appeals on July 30, 2026, less than 24 hours after a hearing where 100+ residents packed City Hall and spilled onto the lawn. The developer's remaining path is an appeal in Lorain County Common Pleas Court.

name: Hexa Builders data center (Black Horse Pike)
note: Previously-approved warehouse project at 3043 South Black Horse Pike amended in early April 2026 to include a 1,000,000 sq ft data center. Two weeks later the township council stripped data-center permissions from the site and banned data centers township-wide; the planning board then deemed the amended application incomplete. Hexa is now suing the township for $300M+. Not dead - the litigation decides it.

name: Project Taurus (Raeden)
note: Retrofit of an existing building on Garden of the Gods Road into the city's first AI data center, by California-based Raeden. Administratively approved by city staff in June 2026; the planning commission denied residents' appeals after a marathon hearing; two new appeals now send it to City Council, whose hearing must fall between Aug 29 and Sept 28 (likely mid-September - date not yet set). Chelsea Glen neighbors cite power, water, and noise from a prior Bitcoin operation at the site.

name: Deep Green downtown data center
note: 24 MW data center plus a 16 MW fuel-cell plant on 2.5 acres near the Grand River downtown, with a closed-loop water-glycol cooling system (~500,000 gal/yr). The Planning Commission recommended the rezoning 5-2 in March 2026, but Deep Green withdrew its rezoning request on April 6, 2026, ending the proposal before a council vote.

name: Stargate Abilene
note: The flagship Stargate site, built by Crusoe on Lancium's Clean Campus - the most complete Stargate location, with roughly four of eight buildings operational (~0.3 GW live) as of mid-2026. OpenAI and Oracle capped the site at 1.2 GW in March 2026, dropping further expansion amid grid-interconnection delays exceeding a year. Power is a mix of on-site natural gas and grid supply.

name: EdgeCore Shannon Hill campus
note: 697 acres purchased in the Shannon Hill Regional Business Park for a 3.9M sq ft, 1.1+ GW campus - a $17B+ investment announced June 2025, phased over several years. No construction start date or tenants disclosed at announcement. Part of a data-center surge in a small county that already hosts an AWS campus.

name: Google West Texas campuses
note: Part of Google's $40B Texas investment through 2027: AI data-center campuses in Haskell County (one paired with a new Intersect/TPG solar + battery storage plant) and Armstrong County, plus additional sites in Pampa and Wilbarger Counties. Company-owned and proceeding, not a contested local rezoning.

name: Augusta Township data center (Thor Equities)
note: The township board rezoned 500+ acres of farmland near Milan from agricultural to general industrial for a hyperscale data center by NY-based Thor Equities. Residents petitioned the decision onto the ballot and voters overturned the rezoning 89.5%-10.4% on Aug 4, 2026 — a rare referendum defeat of an already-approved data-center rezoning.

name: Astra data center campus (Digital Realty)
note: Digital Realty bought ~1,435 acres in the Astra Enterprise Park (the former Sunflower Army Ammunition Plant) to develop a ~600 MW campus across Astra North and South; first phase ~$4B excluding equipment, customer undisclosed. The second major data center proposed near the $4B Panasonic battery plant.

name: Posey County data center (Boberg/Hoenert Roads)
locality: Posey County (Boberg & Hoenert Roads, near Mount Vernon)
note: Commissioners stated at an Aug 4, 2026 meeting in Mount Vernon that they will vote no on the proposed data center near Boberg and Hoenert Roads, while continuing to evaluate proposals elsewhere in the county. The developer is unnamed; commissioners disclosed they signed an NDA despite no official proposal. Residents submitted hundreds of opposition letters and requested a two-year moratorium; no formal vote has been reported.

name: Project Zora
note: Developer controls roughly 1,200 acres of reclaimed mine land in northern Warrick County; the preliminary concept would develop about 300 acres and leave 900 as buffer. County officials met the Project Zora development team on July 30, 2026, emphasizing no votes, commitments, or NDAs were signed and that the developer's capacity/cost claims are unverified. The end user is expected to be publicly identified by end of 2026, with no permit applications before January 2027; commissioners held an Aug 11, 2026 special meeting on data-center zoning-code amendments.

name: AWS Northern Indiana expansion (New Carlisle)
note: Amazon plans a $15B investment in new Northern Indiana data center campuses, additional to the $11B investment announced the prior year in St. Joseph County, where its New Carlisle data center already operates. Amazon secures 2.4 GW for its needs (3 GW total new grid capacity) and, through NIPSCO Generation LLC arrangements, will pay to use existing power lines and cover new power plant costs. Amazon says the expansion creates 1,100+ direct high-skilled jobs.

name: Project Flex
note: Verrus (with Walbridge as general contractor) is developing the Project Flex data center on Milford Road in Lyon Township. The Planning Commission gave initial approval on Sept 8, 2025; final site-plan approval review is anticipated at the commission's Aug 24, 2026 meeting. Verrus is offering a $10M community benefits package and its attorney has warned of legal action if approval is further delayed; residents organized as 'No Data Center Lyon Township' oppose the project.

name: TeraWulf Cayuga data center (former Cayuga Power Plant)
note: TeraWulf leases 183 acres of the 434-acre former Cayuga Power Plant site on Cayuga Lake in Lansing, NY, proposing ~125 acres of development: Phase 1 of 150 MW across three buildings plus a Phase 2 of another 150 MW. On April 27, 2026 the Lansing Planning Board deemed the site-plan application incomplete and requested lease details, construction-traffic data, and landscaping clarification; environmental groups' lawsuit over the Zoning Board's permit interpretation survived a standing challenge on April 29.

name: Dickerson Data Center Campus (Atmosphere)
note: Atmosphere Data Centers (which took over the project from Terra Innovations, whose initial conditional-use application dates to January 2024) proposes a five-building data center campus on 110 acres at the decommissioned Dickerson Generating Station coal plant site; a major modification to the conditional use was filed in December 2025 and amended plans are on Montgomery Planning's development database. On 2026-07-28 the Montgomery County Council approved an 18-month moratorium on new data center approvals that encompasses this proposal; Office of Zoning and Administrative Appeals hearings had been scheduled for Sept 10-11, 2026.

name: Project Double Reed (Stream US Data Centers at STAMP)
note: Stream US Data Centers proposes a $19.46 billion, three-building, roughly 600 MW data center campus at the STAMP site in the Town of Alabama, Genesee County. The Town Planning Board reviewed site-plan conditions (annual noise monitoring, heat-island mitigation, a dedicated code enforcement officer) and was expected to vote July 6, but both July meetings were cancelled after GCEDC, the SEQRA lead agency, could not complete environmental-review documentation; the next scheduled Planning Board meeting was Aug 3, 2026. GCEDC's CEO says the project keeps moving unless New York's passed-but-unsigned statewide data center moratorium becomes law.

name: Stonebridge Associates data center campus at Powder Mill Works
note: Maryland-based Stonebridge Associates has applied to build a data center campus at the Powder Mill Works commercial development site spanning North Beaver and Mahoning townships in Lawrence County, PA. The application was rejected administratively because a required $3,000 Lawrence County escrow check was missing, and back-to-back zoning hearings in early August 2026 argued over whether the application was validly filed - which determines whether older April or newer June zoning rules apply. The zoning board deferred its ruling, expected within 45 days.

name: Prime Data Centers — Starpointe Business Park campus
note: Prime Data Centers filed a conditional-use application in May 2026 for a seven-building, ~1.7 million sq ft data center campus with an attached behind-the-meter 450 MW gas-fired power plant on roughly 126 acres of reclaimed strip-mine land in the Starpointe Business Park (land owned by ALTIAN Development LLC), near the Pavilion at Starlake. The Aug. 5 conditional-use hearing drew 200+ residents; about three dozen won party status, and residents' attorneys argued the application belongs before the zoning hearing board rather than the supervisors, so the hearing was continued to Aug. 31 without Prime presenting.

name: 900 Conshohocken Road data center (former Cleveland-Cliffs steel mill)
note: 900 Conshohocken Road LLC, an entity of developer Brian O'Neill, seeks a special exception from Plymouth Township's zoning hearing board to convert the recently closed Cleveland-Cliffs steel mill — 10 existing buildings totaling about 2 million sq ft on 66 acres along the Schuylkill River — into a data center. The Aug. 6 hearing nearly filled a 750-seat auditorium; Conshohocken Borough was granted party status while Norristown was denied. The board set a procedural-only session for Aug. 17, with testimony continuing in September; an opposition petition has topped 4,000 signatures.

name: AWS Salem Township campus (Susquehanna nuclear plant)
note: One of two initial sites in Amazon's announced $20B+ Pennsylvania data-center investment: a campus alongside the Susquehanna Steam Electric Station nuclear plant, where majority owner Talen Energy agreed to supply 960 MW. The original behind-the-meter connection drew FERC scrutiny and was blocked in 2024. The 960 MW figure is the contracted power supply, not built capacity.

name: AWS Falls Township campus (Keystone Trade Center)
note: Second initial site of Amazon's $20B+ Pennsylvania investment: a data center at NorthPoint Development's Keystone Trade Center (1,800-acre former U.S. Steel Fairless Works site), including conversion of a planned 1M sq ft distribution building on a 247-acre parcel at 1 Ben Fairless Drive and a broader ~2M sq ft, 10-structure digital infrastructure campus. Falls Township supervisors approved revised preliminary/final land development plans for the data center use in March 2025.

name: Social Circle data center complex (Fairplay Drive / Roy Malcom Road tracts)
note: A data center complex assembled from three tracts totaling more than 450 acres on the southeast side of Fairplay Drive and Roy Malcom Road, from Social Circle Parkway to Hawkins Academy Road. The Social Circle Planning Commission voted unanimously at a called April 2026 meeting to recommend annexation, rezoning, special-use permitting and a future land use map change for the final 123-acre tract at 1402 Roy Malcom Road (concept plan: two buildings of about 248,600 sq ft each); the city council then approved all four requests 3-0 at a meeting reported May 1, 2026. Engineering firm Thomas & Hutton represents the property owner; project representatives say an unnamed 'end user' is already lined up and construction could begin in fall 2026.

name: Project Red and Project Yellow
filing_llc: National CRE Holdings LLC; Greenland Capital LLC
note: Two proposed data center campuses covering 677 acres on the grounds of the existing Wolf Hollow power generating complex in Hood County. District Judge Bryan Bufkin of the 355th Judicial District Court granted the county's plea to the jurisdiction and dismissed with prejudice the developers' suit arguing the projects were automatically approved because the county missed a 30-day statutory deadline; the judge found the submissions did not meet the state's definition of 'development plans.' Commissioners had twice delayed voting on the projects pending more disclosure and compliance with new county development regulations. Reporting identifies National CRE Holdings LLC as a Starwood Capital Group entity and Greenland Capital LLC as the owner of MARA Holdings, which already operates two bitcoin mining sites in the county.

name: Vantage Frontier
note: Vantage Data Centers' largest campus and investment to date: a $25 billion, 1.4 GW AI campus on 1,200 acres in Shackelford County, Texas, comprising 10 data centers totaling 3.7 million square feet. Construction was already underway at announcement, with the first building scheduled for delivery in the second half of 2026 and more than 5,000 construction and operations jobs projected. Vantage says the campus uses liquid cooling with a closed-loop chiller system requiring minimal water. No tenant is identified in the announcement.

name: AWS Madison County data center campuses
note: AWS announced on 2024-01-25 a $10 billion investment and at least 1,000 jobs to build data center complexes in two Madison County industrial parks, then the largest capital investment in Mississippi history. On 2026-04-09 Amazon announced an additional $11 billion Madison County expansion and 700 more jobs, part of a $25 billion statewide total (also covering $3 billion in Warren County/Vicksburg and $1 billion at the former Delphi plant in Clinton, Hinds County) and more than 2,000 jobs. No per-campus megawatt or acreage figure is given in the sources fetched.

name: Monticello Tech data center campus
note: Monticello Tech, led by Frattalone Companies CEO Nick Frattalone, filed a land-use application with the City of Monticello, Minnesota on 2026-07-07 seeking rezoning to a Data Center Planned Unit Development district plus preliminary plat and conditional use permit approvals for a site south of 85th Street NE and east of Highway 25. The application describes 547 acres (364 developable), up to 3 million sq ft, as many as 8 principal buildings, about 75,000 gallons/day of water, and a connection to Xcel Energy's 345 kV system; the developer projects about $7 million in annual property tax at full buildout, with construction possibly starting Q1 2028. The eventual operator is not identified. City staff had until 2026-08-21 to determine whether the application is complete; Minnesota law then allows a 60-day review, extendable to 120 days.

name: Antelope Data Campus (Project Antelope)
note: Iron County Planning Commission unanimously approved a conditional use permit on 2026-06-04 for Pronghorn Development LLC's five-building campus (up to 6.75M sq ft, with an on-site natural gas plant of up to 1.5 GW) on 640 acres along Antelope Springs Road, about 8 miles west of Cedar City, with 62 conditions covering water rights, wastewater, noise, lighting and site restoration. The application was vested before a county moratorium on new data center applications adopted the month prior; additional permits are still required before construction. Buildout is proposed in phases over 8-10 years.

name: Stratos
note: O'Leary Digital, chaired by Kevin O'Leary, proposes the Stratos campus in unincorporated Box Elder County near Brigham City: eleven 100 MW data center buildings plus a 7.5-9 GW natural gas plant and a 500 MW solar array on roughly 40,000 acres across three sites. Renderings were released 2026-05-19; the county commission approved an interlocal agreement with the Military Installation Development Authority in early May 2026. State environmental permitting could take about two years, with a 30-day public comment period and hearing required, and over 40 protests have been filed on its water rights application.

name: QTS Cedar Rapids Data Center Campus
note: QTS (a Blackstone portfolio company) is building a seven-building campus on 612 acres of Alliant Energy's Big Cedar Industrial Center; the Cedar Rapids City Council approved the development agreement with QTS Cedar Rapids LLC on 2025-01-28 with a minimum $750M investment, later announced by QTS as a $10B campus. The agreement includes up to $18M over 20 years to a Community Betterment Fund, tax increment financing rebates, and water-free cooling; the development agreement requires construction to begin within three years and finish within six.

name: Compass Datacenters Red Oak campus
note: Red Oak City Council voted 4-1 to rezone ~830 acres of agricultural land ~20 miles south of Dallas to a planned development for a Compass data center campus of nearly a dozen buildings plus substations, after a marathon May 11 meeting that ran past midnight with 150+ residents present and ~1,600 petition signatures against; the planning and zoning board had recommended denial in late April. Conditions include lighting shields, decibel limits, a cryptocurrency-mining ban, closed-loop cooling with no city water draw, and $72 million in electric grid reinforcements; a 10-year, $2.82 million tax abatement passed on a separate 4-1 vote.

name: BCG Cedar Creek Campus
note: Black Chamber Partners (a BlackChamber Group affiliate) and co-developer Pacifico Energy plan a 2,842-acre data center campus at 382 Earl Callahan Road near Cedar Creek with a 710 MW gas-fired energy facility, a ~$2.2 billion investment with two 100% county tax-abatement applications under review; construction is estimated for September 2026 through October 2028. Neighboring property owners filed motions July 20 asking TCEQ to overturn two construction stormwater permits issued in mid-July.

name: Amazon Fort Stockton campus
note: Amazon Data Services filed TDLR registrations for three data center buildings (A, B, C; 189,060 sq ft and ~$300 million each) at a site 11 miles north of Fort Stockton, with construction scheduled August-December 2026, part of an August 2026 filing wave totaling 16 buildings and at least $4.8 billion across Fort Stockton, Floydada, and Amazon's existing Boling (Wharton County) campus. Amazon confirmed it is financing the GW Ranch gas plant being developed by Pacifico Energy in Pecos County (35 turbines, 7.65 GW) to power the campus; its permitted emissions of over 30 million metric tonnes of GHG per year would exceed any single source currently operating in the US.

name: Amazon Floydada campus
note: Amazon Data Services filed TDLR registrations for three data center buildings (B, C, D; 189,060 sq ft and ~$300 million each) near Floydada, about 45 miles northeast of Lubbock, with construction planned August 2026 through April 2027. The filings were part of an August 2026 wave totaling 16 buildings and at least $4.8 billion across Floydada, a new Fort Stockton (Pecos County) campus, and six added buildings at Amazon's existing Boling (Wharton County) campus.

name: Manse Technology Campus (formerly Project Blackjack)
note: Gigawatt Development proposes a ~900-acre, multi-phase technology campus south of Carpenter Canyon Road along SR-160 at the south end of Pahrump Valley, pledging closed-loop cooling using under 300 acre-feet of water per year (~1.5% of the Pahrump Basin's annual yield) on water rights it already owns, with no tax abatements sought; the application predates the county's June 2026 temporary moratorium on new data center applications. The 'August vote' was on Nye County Bill 2026-11, a proposed ban on data centers in communities without elected town boards: at the Aug 4 commission meeting it did not come to a vote, and commissioners instead moved toward putting the question to voters, with a possible special election (earliest January 2027) to be discussed Aug 18.

name: Monarch Data Center
note: Lyon County commissioners voted 3-1 (Commissioner Hockaday opposed; Commissioner Cassinelli abstained) to approve the planned unit development rezoning for Copia Power's ~505-acre, 4.6 million sq ft, 1,000 MW Monarch campus in Mason Valley north of Yerington, which includes a 500 MW natural-gas backup plant and battery energy storage, after 6+ hours of comment from a mostly opposed crowd of nearly 300. The approval covers zoning only: final PUD/design approval, Nevada Division of Environmental Protection and State Engineer permits, and completion of Copia's land purchase remain, and tribal members vowed legal action over cultural resources and sacred sites.

name: Green Data Socorro campus (New Mexico Tech land)
owner: New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology (proposed site)
note: Green Data Centers CEO Jason Bak proposed a 10,000-acre campus on New Mexico Tech land west of M Mountain and north of Highway 60 outside Socorro, powered by a 10 GW solar array delivering ~2 GW of base-load power, with atmospheric water generation for a water-neutral design; it was unveiled March 25, 2026 at a Socorro Electric Cooperative board meeting. After a raucous May town hall, New Mexico Tech announced June 2 it would not move forward, saying it lacks sufficient contiguous, undeveloped parcels for the ~16-square-mile footprint. Socorro County commissioners then unanimously adopted a one-year moratorium on data centers and supporting infrastructure on June 9.

name: Terra Nexus data center campus (316 Old Cheraw Highway)
filing_llc: Terra Nexus Land Fund I, LLC
note: Terra Nexus Land Fund I, LLC asked Rockingham to rezone ~165 acres at 316 Old Cheraw Highway from high-density residential (R-7) to conditional light industrial for a $1.2B, ~30-job data center campus — Richmond County's third. The Planning Board unanimously recommended approval on Aug 4; a City Council public hearing must precede any vote, but fetched coverage (as of Aug 13) gives no confirmed hearing date.

name: 1155 Powers Ferry Place data center (Prime Storage site)
note: Marietta City Council voted 5-2 on Aug 12, 2026 to approve rezoning for an 18 MW, 90,000 sq ft data center at Prime Storage's ~11-acre Powers Ferry Place property near I-75 and Delk Road — the city's second data center. Conditions include silencers on coolers/generators, an independent sound study, no connection to municipal water, and Prime Storage agreeing not to build data centers at its other Marietta sites. The application predated the six-month moratorium the council passed July 8.

name: Stillwater data center campus (Panhandle Road)
note: Stillwater Development's 15-building, 3.5 million sq ft campus at 11760 Panhandle Road — 1.25 GW at full build, sited across from Michelle Obama Elementary and Eddie White Middle school traffic — was withdrawn at an Aug 6, 2026 council meeting after strong community opposition; plans were first filed in December 2025. The developer is pivoting to residential development, and Mayor Marci Fluellyn said the city will begin updating its zoning to prohibit data centers.

name: Mason County hyperscale data center campus
note: The Mason County Fiscal Court gave final approval on May 22, 2026 to rezone 28 properties (2,080 acres, A-2 agricultural to I-3 industrial) outside Maysville for a hyperscale data center campus; the application's development plan shows six data center buildings, three utility substations, and 15 detention ponds on ~1,975 net acres. The developer's identity remains undisclosed, and a legal challenge by residents group We Are Mason County was pending at approval.

name: Baconton power generation facility (data-center-linked, NextEra-linked)
note: On June 29, 2026 Mitchell County commissioners rezoned ~300 acres of agricultural land to industrial near Baconton, clearing the way for a 1,500 MW power generation facility linked in reporting to NextEra Energy and described by residents as intended to supply data centers across southwest Georgia — the rezoned project is a power plant, not a data center itself (size_mw is generation capacity). Residents are pursuing a referendum on the rezoning, a one-year data center moratorium petition, and recalls of commissioners.

name: Cave City data center (Kentucky Industrial Alliance)
note: Kentucky Industrial Alliance LLC proposes a data center on a 381-acre project site within its 600+ acres at 2001 Doyle Avenue, about 10 miles from Mammoth Cave National Park; it submitted an application May 11, 2026, and sued the city on June 8 after Cave City adopted a one-year moratorium. The city moved to dismiss on June 29, arguing no actual development plan was ever filed; a July 20 preliminary-injunction hearing was scheduled. Residents fear runoff through the karst into the Mammoth Cave system.

name: Project Delta
note: Hyperscale data center on 1,800 acres near Dan River; 998 acres developable, rest is floodplain. Originally approved by commissioners Jan 2026 but rescinded in April after a lawsuit (SCSJ/SELC) challenged the public hearing notice. ELS reapplied in late July 2026. Planning board voted 5-2 to recommend denial on Aug 14, 2026. Commissioners make the final decision. Closed-loop cooling and possible on-site generation planned.

name: Smithfield Gateway Data Center
operator: DEPG Mosier Associates LP / DEPG of Shawnee II LP
note: Two 250,000 sq ft data center buildings proposed at Smithfield Gateway behind St. Luke's and Wawa on Route 209. Developer filed a curative amendment application; township initiated a 180-day review period starting May 6, 2026. Township is proposing a new H-1 (Heavy Industrial) Zoning District where data centers would be the only permitted conditional use, removing them from ED and M-1 districts. Board of Supervisors held public hearing and vote on Aug 12, 2026.

name: Energence Utah Digital Infrastructure Campus
note: Massive 5,046-acre multi-use campus with 475-acre data center area (expandable to 1,000+ acres), 200-acre energy center, and ~1,440 acres of solar. Targets 100 MW by Year 2, 700 MW by Year 4, up to 1.2 GW firm / 1.9 GW total by Year 6. Senmiao Technology (NASDAQ: AIHS) entered a non-binding LOI for $5M staged investment for 51% equity in Energence Utah. Campus already has active conditional-use permits and 100,000 MMBTU/day gas commitment. Very early stage (LOI, not binding) and highly speculative given micro-cap sponsor.

name: Andover HPC Data Center
note: National Land Developers registered Andover HPC Development in December 2025 at 248 Stickles Pond Road, a 97-acre former airport site. Andover Township first allowed data centers in a redevelopment zone along Route 206 (September 2025) and raised the height limit to 65 feet (April 2026), but after a chaotic May 2026 meeting with 300 residents, the township passed Ordinance 2026-13 banning data centers township-wide. No formal site plan was ever filed. National Land Developers sued in Sussex County Superior Court on July 10, 2026, challenging the ban.

name: Pennhurst Data Center Campus
note: Penn Hurst Holdings proposed a 1.9 million-square-foot data center campus on 123 acres of the historic Pennhurst State School and Hospital site. The East Vincent Township Board of Supervisors voted unanimously to deny the conditional use application on May 21, 2026. Penn Hurst Holdings appealed to Chester County Court of Common Pleas on June 26, arguing irreconcilable contradictions in the township's zoning code.

name: Karis Critical Plum Farms Data Center
note: Karis Critical acquired 180 acres known as Plum Farms at the northwest corner of Route 59 and Higgins Road for $45 million and sought rezoning for a data center. The village planning commission gave a negative recommendation in early June 2026. After weeks of community backlash, Karis notified the village on July 1 that it would withdraw the rezoning request. Governor Pritzker had also suspended state data center incentives. Karis has not indicated whether it will refile.

name: Site Layer 4 Data Center Campus
note: Site Layer 4, a New York-based firm, has applied to rezone 5,344 acres of ranchland on the Lazy V Six Ranch northeast of Wheatland for a $26 billion data center campus with co-located utility-scale energy generation. The project promises 300 jobs and substantial tax revenue but neighbors are concerned about water, wildlife, and viewshed impacts. More than 400 public comments were received. Planning and Zoning Commission hearing rescheduled to August 26, 2026, with County Commissioners hearing on September 2.

name: Project Bluestem
note: Cloverleaf Infrastructure proposes Project Bluestem, a 600 MW hyperscale data center on approximately 1,000 acres of former Tailgate Ranch land south of Tonganoxie. The Leavenworth County Commission passed a 90-day moratorium on data center applications in May 2026, which expired in August. On August 5, commissioners voted 3-2 against extending the moratorium. On August 13, officials reversed course and directed planning and zoning to delay regulation recommendations until after a joint work session before the September meeting. No formal application has been submitted.

name: Muncy Township Data Center
note: DANKO Holdings II / Fishlips LLC filed a zoning permit application on April 15, 2026, and a conditional use application on April 28, for three data center buildings along John Brady Drive near Yetter Road, about two miles east of the closed Lycoming Mall. The township failed to hold the required hearing within 60 days, and the developer published a legal notice in July claiming 'deemed approval' under the state Municipalities Planning Code. Supervisors imposed a nine-month moratorium on data center submissions in June 2026. The legal status of the deemed-approval claim is unresolved.

name: Urbana Technology Hub
note: Thor Equities assembled approximately 230 acres near Ohio 55 and US 68 for a 460,000 sq ft, $1B+ data center campus called the Urbana Technology Hub. A site plan application was submitted February 13 but deemed incomplete by city staff. The BZA unanimously denied Thor's appeal. The city council then adopted new zoning codes removing data centers as a permitted use in the M-1 manufacturing district. Thor Equities filed a federal lawsuit in the US District Court for the Southern District of Ohio. A charter amendment petition and mayor recall effort are also underway.

name: Black Mountain Energy Fort Worth
note: 187-acre campus with 980-MW substation off Lon Stephenson Road; approved by Fort Worth Zoning Commission in April 2026 despite neighbor opposition; city later passed a 90-day citywide data center moratorium that exempts already-approved projects.

name: CloudBurst San Marcos
note: Gigawatt-scale gas-powered AI campus straddling Hays and Guadalupe Counties; site sits outside both cities' ETJ to avoid local review. Over 50 residents opposed at San Marcos council meetings over water scarcity, emissions and transparency.

name: Sabey Decatur Township
note: Two-building, 900,000+ sq ft, $4B campus near Camby Rd/Kentucky Ave. Approved by Metropolitan Development Commission in March 2026 via industrial-zoning adjustment; ~90 residents protested. Residents later sued; case helped drive Indianapolis's data-center moratorium push.

name: PORTS Technology Campus (SoftBank)
note: Leased land on DOE's former Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant site. Billed as potentially world's largest AI data center at 10GW full buildout (phase 1 is 800MW), paired with 9.2GW on-site gas plant ($33.3B) and $4.2B in new AEP Ohio transmission.

name: Project Bluegrass (Panattoni)
note: Developer sought annexation into City of Burgin to escape Mercer County's one-year data center moratorium; residents cited environmental and utility-rate concerns.

name: CoreSite DE3 (Denver)
note: 170,000 sq ft facility at 5050 N. Race St drawing 65-75MW. Under construction with no required community notice; opposition from the neighborhood was the direct catalyst for Denver's citywide one-year data center moratorium passed in May 2026.

name: Matrix Data Center Campus
note: $18.7B, 1,677-acre, 3GW net-zero AI campus on former Thermo lignite mine land. Phase I: 390 acres/800MW across 8 buildings; Phase II adds geothermal microgrid by 2027.

name: Bradenton Crossings Data Center
note: 35-acre mixed development at 202 13th Ave E; data-center piece withdrawn July 2026. The withdrawal plus utility-strain concerns prompted county commissioners to draft a countywide data center moratorium ordinance.

name: Compass Wakarusa Campus
note: 10-building data center campus proposed on ~600 acres of light-industrial land southwest of Topeka; conditional use permit filed July 24, 2026, county flagged application 'incomplete' Aug 4.

name: DataBank Project Indo
note: 200MW, $2.4B, 1.1M sq ft data center campus at 218 Industrial Park Road near Atlanta; filed a Development of Regional Impact application and a 288MW grid interconnection request.

name: Aligned Shippingport (Project Phoenix)
note: Nearly 2M sq ft, ~$10B natural-gas-powered data center campus on the former Bruce Mansfield coal plant site; land deal ($223.15M) closed July 29, 2026.

name: Talen Energy Montour Data Center
note: County commissioners unanimously denied Talen Energy's request to rezone 800+ acres from agricultural to industrial for a data center plus power-plant expansion, after a grassroots group gathered ~3,000 petition signatures.

name: Flexential Kaufman County
note: Fourth and largest Flexential DFW-area facility; 110-acre site supports up to three 36MW buildings (108MW total); Phase 1 is 375,000 sq ft / 36MW, site work starting early 2027.

name: Iron Mountain Hutto Campus
note: Seven-building data center campus proposed outside Austin near the Samsung Taylor plant, with on-site substation; exploring behind-the-meter natural gas to speed up power availability.

name: T5@ATL IV (Palmetto)
note: New multi-building Atlanta-area campus scalable to 300MW with on-site substation, expected operational in 2026.

name: NTT VA11 Gainesville
note: 96MW/300,000 sq ft facility (VA11) as first phase of a planned 336MW campus, due live early 2027; part of $10B+ NTT US buildout.

name: DataBank Red Oak Campus
note: 8-building campus (400MW substation, up to 300MW critical IT); first 3 buildings already leased, $2.0B construction financing secured April 2026.

name: CloudHQ Mount Prospect
note: Village hired outside engineering firm to handle CloudHQ's permit reviews; also set up a dedicated public fact-check portal, signaling active community scrutiny.

name: Vantage NV1 (Storey County)
note: Vantage's entry into the Nevada market; 224MW campus, first two buildings fully leased, first building opening Q2 2026.

name: Vantage VA4 Fredericksburg
note: $2B, 192MW hyperscale campus (VA4); first building scheduled to open late 2027.

name: Fort Meade Data Center Campus
note: 4.4M sq ft hyperscale campus on former phosphate-mine land, $2.6-2.8B investment; city commissioners approved developer agreement April 14, 2026.

name: Atlas Capital Bloomfield
note: Proposed 1M-sq-ft data center at 132 Griffin Road North; surfaced at a June 26, 2026 Town Plan and Zoning Commission meeting.

name: NE Edge Millstone (Waterford)
note: 1.5M-sq-ft data center proposed to draw power directly from Millstone nuclear plant; host-fee agreement lapsed after nearly 3 years of local opposition, effectively ending the project.

name: Quantica Big Sky Campus
note: 5,000-acre campus; NorthWestern Energy committed up to 1,000 MW to Quantica as of July 2026, with Phase I construction slated for 2026.

name: Applied Digital Deuel County (withdrawn)
note: $5B, 430MW campus near Toronto, SD; withdrawn after 2026 legislature rejected a sales-tax exemption for data centers.

name: Gemini Sioux Falls Technology Park
note: 500MW hyperscale campus on 164 acres next to Xcel's Split Rock Substation; received unanimous rezoning approval from Sioux Falls City Council on January 6, 2026.

name: Microsoft Cheyenne Expansion
note: Microsoft announced intent to acquire ~3,200 acres in southeast Cheyenne for a multiyear data-center expansion, building on its Black Hills Energy partnership.

name: STAK Energy North Slope Campus
note: $500M, up to 3GW natural-gas-powered AI data center campus on 715 leased acres ~26 mi south of Deadhorse; received preliminary state land-lease approval, construction targeted summer 2026.

name: Imperial Valley Data Center
note: ~950,000-1M sq ft AI/ML data center; county supervisors approved it in April 2026 then reversed course, imposing a 45-day moratorium after water-use and air-quality opposition; developer sued over the moratorium.

name: Goodman Innovation Centre San Jose
note: Two-building, 414,000 sq ft data center campus (97MW) on 45.8-acre infill site bought for $200M; expected operational 2028.

name: Valar Atomics Orangeville SMR
note: Nearly-waterless 30MW AI data center powered by Valar's Ward250 small modular reactor with Nvidia's direct liquid cooling.

name: Drox Group Rural Hall
note: 129-acre hyperscale campus; Planning Board recommended denying rezoning despite developer concessions ($80M projected tax revenue over 10 years).

name: Mountain Road Technology Park
note: 427-acre, five-building campus; up to 2M gal/day water peak. Planning Commission approved 6-1 (Apr 16) but Board of Supervisors denied rezoning, height exception, and substation permit 4-3 (May 27, 2026).

name: Project Spero

name: Saxum Investment Data Center

name: Google Hermantown Campus

name: 100 Jersey Avenue AI Data Center
